specification.problem: Physical mapping of fault-tolerant quantum circuits: jointly handle operation scheduling, placement and qubit routing to minimize circuit latency, and select the single best Universal Logic Block (ULB) size for a target circuit by weighting per-operation latencies by their critical-path frequency.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Classical CAD-style mapping flow (loose force-directed scheduling, timing-driven placement, dynamic routing latency) plus ULB size selection. Not a quantum algorithm with a state-preparation or measurement circuit; only a tiny finite weighted-latency illustration is reconstructed. Specific force formulas, cost functions and benchmarks are not in the abstract.

specification.initial_state: No quantum state; input is a quantum data flow graph of a target FT circuit and a set of candidate ULB sizes.

steps.description: Loose scheduling: transform the initial QDFG into one that explicitly captures no-cloning, then run modified force-directed scheduling to reduce resource contention and latency.
Placement: timing-driven placement minimizing approximate routing latencies, iteratively calling the force-directed scheduler to correct scheduling levels.
Routing: compute dynamic routing latencies for qubits given the placement.
ULB sizing: map FT operations onto each candidate ULB size, weight latencies by critical-path frequency, and choose the minimizing size.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute weighted latency L_s per candidate size and pick the argmin; the 40% latency reduction is a reported result, not a derived formula.
assumptions: Weighted-sum latency model is an assumed instance
Registers describe classical data structures, not qubit registers
The mapping flow is classical, so there is no quantum measurement
